report.source_text: Microscopically, at low magnification (Fig. 2A), the tumor cells were diffusely distributed in patchy areas, with areas of hemorrhage, necrosis, and indistinct margins blending with adjacent tissues. At medium magnification (Fig. 2B), the cells exhibited fusiform and ovoid shapes, arranged in sheets or bundles. High magnification analysis revealed that the tumor comprised round to epithelioid cells (Fig. 2C), which were monomorphic and loosely cohesive, with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. In some areas, rhabdoid tumor cells (Fig. 2D) were observed, characterized by cytoplasmic inclusions, eccentric nuclei, active mitotic figures, and the presence of giant tumor cells. Geographic necrosis was also present, with numerous apoptotic bodies interspersed among the tumor cells and granular blue-stained nuclear debris.

The surface of the mass was smooth, with a wide and firm base. The mass exerted significant compression on the intestine, causing incomplete intestinal obstruction and proximal intestine dilation. Postoperatively, the excised tissue was sent for pathological examination.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old male smoker presented with acute onset right-sided abdominal pain, distention, nausea, and a single episode of vomiting lasting more than 4 days. Physical examination revealed a palpable 3.0 × 2.8 cm non-tender movable mass in the right abdomen at the umbilical level with mild tenderness but no peritoneal signs. CT imaging demonstrated a 41 × 37 mm high-density mass in the right lower abdomen with surface enhancement, closely associated with the small intestine, causing mechanical small bowel obstruction with proximal dilation and multiple fluid levels. Exploratory laparotomy revealed an irregular 5 × 3 cm mass located 180 cm distal to Treitz's ligament adjacent to the intestinal mesentery with a smooth surface and firm base, causing incomplete intestinal obstruction. Partial small bowel resection and anastomosis were performed. Histopathological examination showed an undifferentiated mesenchymal tumor with monomorphic round to epithelioid cells, rhabdoid features, active mitotic figures, geographic necrosis, and hemorrhage. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated BRG1 negativity (indicating SMARCA4 loss), Vimentin positivity, CD34 positivity, and high Ki-67 proliferation index (80%), with extensive negativity for other markers (CK7, TTF1, P40, Bcl-2, CD15, CD20, CD3, CD21, CD30, c-Myc, cyclin D1, HMB45, Melan-A, MUM1, EMA, CD117, CDX2, Dog-1, SDH, INI-1, SMA, calretinin, WT1, CD31, F8, ERG, Fli-1, galectin 3, and hepatocyte markers). The final pathological diagnosis confirmed SMARCA4-UT originating in the small mesentery. Postoperatively, the patient received symptomatic treatment including anti-infection measures, hemostasis, fluid replacement, and nutritional support, which alleviated the intestinal obstruction symptoms and allowed hospital discharge.
